DECK: Discipleship Experience (Section 12) Church History

Q1. Which distinction does the lesson on Baptism make between the Lutheran and Reformed positions?
A. Lutherans reject infant baptism, while Reformed churches require it for salvation.
B. Lutherans view baptism as a means of grace, while the Reformed view baptism as a seal of God's covenant.
C. Both groups teach that baptism is purely symbolic and has no relationship to grace.
D. Both groups reject infant baptism because personal faith must always precede baptism.
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: The Lutheran Church teaches that baptism is a means of grace, whereas the Reformed position views it as a symbolic sign and seal of God's covenant.
REF: BAPTISM II — [04:52], [06:15] - [07:48]

Q2. What did the Nicene Creed affirm in the controversy described in the lesson on Church History?
A. That salvation comes through secret knowledge
B. That Jesus was adopted as God's Son
C. The divinity of Christ
D. That the Father, Son and Holy Spirit are three modes of one person
ANSWER: C
REF: JESUS-SON-OF-MAN-II — [04:47–05:43]

Q3. What does Acts 10:2 contribute to the lesson's teaching about sacrifice?
A. Cornelius' prayers and alms were presented as having come up as a memorial before God.
B. Cornelius' financial giving was the only reason the angel appeared to him.
C. Cornelius' sacrifice made him born again before the gospel was preached to him.
D. Cornelius' alms were presented as more important than his prayer life.
ANSWER: A
EXPLANATION: Acts 10 reveals that Cornelius' prayers and sacrificial giving (alms) came up together as a memorial before God, attracting angelic visitation.
REF: HOW TO ATTRACT ANGELS V — [05:23] - [06:29]
BIBLE: Confirmed in lesson and deck: Acts 10:2 <https://www.esv.org/verses/Acts+10%3A2/>

Q4. What did Pelagius teach that the church rejected?
A. Humans could live sinless lives without the aid of divine grace.
B. Salvation could only come through hidden knowledge.
C. Jesus was not truly human.
D. God exists in three distinct persons.
ANSWER: A

Q5. Cornelius had not been born again, was not full of the Spirit and most likely had never read a book about angels. What does his example establish?
A. Knowledge about angels is not necessary for a life of reverence to God.
B. Angelic encounters only happen to people outside the church.
C. A person must first understand spiritual realities before God can engage with him.
D. Being outside the church automatically makes a person more sensitive to angels.
ANSWER: A
EXPLANATION: Cornelius proves that a person can attract angelic ministry purely through a lifestyle of genuine reverence and the fear of the Lord, without prior theological knowledge of angels.
REF: HOW TO ATTRACT ANGELS I — [13:17] - [14:06]; HOW TO ATTRACT ANGELS II — [03:27] - [04:50]
BIBLE: Also cited in lesson segment: Psalm 34:7 <https://www.esv.org/verses/Psalm+34%3A7/>

Q6. Which sequence best supports the lesson's argument that Christianity's roots in Africa go back beyond the colonial era?
A. Portuguese explorers arrived in Africa, missionaries followed them, and African kingdoms adopted Christianity.
B. Jesus fled to Egypt, Simon of Cyrene carried Jesus' cross, and the Ethiopian eunuch heard the gospel and was baptised.
C. Constantine legalised Christianity, founded Constantinople, and missionaries later travelled to Africa.
D. Martin Luther began the Reformation, the Jesuits expanded Catholicism, and missionaries then entered Africa.
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: Biblical accounts of Jesus fleeing to Egypt, Simon of Cyrene carrying the cross, and the Ethiopian eunuch's conversion prove Christianity has deep African roots predating European colonialism.
REF: EARLY CHURCH II — [06:16] - [07:29]

B. It describes angels as spirits and ministers and is connected to the manifestation of fire.
C. It teaches that angels can only minister through fire.
D. It shows that angels are symbols rather than actual spiritual beings.
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: Psalm 104:4 establishes that God makes His angels spirits and ministers, which the lesson connects directly to angelic manifestations of fire.

B. Being baptized by immersion
C. Believing loyalty
D. Being recognized by a church leader as a believer
ANSWER: C
EXPLANATION: True salvation is evidenced not merely by a temporary profession of faith, but by a consistent "believing loyalty" that endures.

Q9. What was Arius' main argument concerning Jesus?
A. Jesus was not divine in the same way as the Father and was not co-eternal.
B. Jesus was only a human prophet and never existed before His birth.
C. Jesus was fully divine and co-eternal with the Father.
D. Jesus became God's Son only after His resurrection.
ANSWER: A
REF: JESUS-SON-OF-MAN-II — [04:47–05:43]

Q10. What did Docetism teach about Jesus?
A. Jesus was fully human but was adopted as God's Son later in His life.
B. Jesus was one person appearing in three different modes.
C. Jesus was divine but was not the same as the Father.
D. Jesus only appeared to be human, so His body, suffering and death were considered illusions.
ANSWER: D
EXPLANATION: Docetism is the heretical belief that Jesus only appeared to be human, treating His physical body, suffering, and death as mere illusions.
REF: EARLY CHURCH I — [04:52]
BIBLE: Added from online research: John 1:14 <https://www.esv.org/verses/John+1%3A14/>

Q11. What connection does Daniel 10:12 establish between prayer and angelic activity in the lesson?
A. Daniel's prayer was heard, and the angel said he had come because of his words.
B. Daniel's angel came because Daniel had achieved a high level of spiritual maturity.
C. Daniel's experience shows that angels respond only to prophetic declarations.
D. Daniel's experience shows that prayer becomes unnecessary once an angel is assigned to a person.
ANSWER: A
EXPLANATION: Daniel 10:12 illustrates that angels respond to the prayers of believers, as the angel explicitly stated he came because of Daniel's words.

Q12. Which set of questions does the lesson identify as the major areas of disagreement surrounding water baptism?
A. Who performs baptism, where it is performed, how often it is performed, and what language is used
B. The mode of baptism, who should be baptized, the purpose of baptism, and whether baptism is regenerative
C. Whether baptism should happen before or after communion, who should administer communion, and whether communion saves
D. Whether baptism should happen publicly, privately, annually, or only after a baptismal class
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: Historically, controversies on water baptism center around its mode, the proper subjects for it, its purpose, and whether it has a regenerative nature.
REF: BAPTISM I — [01:35] - [02:50]

Q13. What role did figures such as Ignatius of Antioch and Irenaeus play?
A. They introduced Christianity to the Roman Empire for the first time.
B. They replaced the apostles as the founders of the Christian faith.
C. They defended Christian doctrine and affirmed the authority of the apostles.
D. They led the Protestant Reformation against the Catholic Church.
ANSWER: C
EXPLANATION: During the second century, early church figures like Ignatius and Irenaeus wrote to defend orthodox Christian doctrine and uphold apostolic authority.

Q14. Why does the lesson describe Abraham's encounter as an "honor test"?

B. Abraham had to respond honorably to what appeared to be an ordinary situation.
C. Abraham was required to perform a special act of worship before the visitors could speak to him.
D. Abraham's encounter depended on him recognising the visitors as angels immediately.
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: Abraham's encounter functioned as an honor test because the divine visitors appeared as ordinary passersby, requiring Abraham to proactively demonstrate honorable hospitality.

B. Growing heresies and false teachings threatened the unity of the faith.
C. The apostles had stopped teaching Christians about Jesus.
D. Christianity had already become the official religion of the Roman Empire.
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: The early church was compelled to solidify its doctrinal beliefs to combat emerging heresies and false teachings that jeopardized their unity.

D. It teaches that baptism is the means by which a person first receives faith.
ANSWER: A

Q22. What did the Edict of Milan accomplish according to the lesson?
A. It legalised Christianity and ended decades of persecution.
B. It made Christianity the only religion in the Roman Empire.
C. It divided Christianity into Eastern and Western churches.
D. It established the Nicene Creed as the official Roman constitution.
ANSWER: A
EXPLANATION: The Edict of Milan in 313 AD officially legalized Christianity and brought an end to decades of state-sponsored persecution.
REF: EARLY CHURCH I — [04:52]

Q23. What sequence of events does the lesson give concerning Constantine?
A. He legalised Christianity, then saw a cross, then became a Christian.
B. He founded Constantinople, then legalised Christianity, then fought his pivotal battle.
C. He saw a cross before a pivotal battle, won the battle, embraced Christianity, and later issued the Edict of Milan.
D. He became a bishop, convened the Council of Nicaea, and then founded Constantinople.
ANSWER: C
EXPLANATION: Constantine first saw a cross before a major battle, emerged victorious, embraced the Christian faith, and subsequently issued the Edict of Milan.
REF: EARLY CHURCH I — [03:46] - [04:52]

Q24. What is the significance of the Greek word baptizo?
A. It is presented as meaning sprinkling, which supports the practice of pouring.
B. It is presented as meaning to immerse or submerge, which supports immersion.
C. It is presented as meaning to cleanse spiritually, which proves baptism regenerates.
D. It is presented as meaning to dedicate an infant to God.
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: The original Greek word "baptizo" explicitly means to immerse, dip, or submerge, linguistically supporting the practice of full-body immersion.
REF: BAPTISM I — [04:05]

D. Salvation comes through human effort without divine grace.

Q28. What is the significance of Ezekiel 36 and 1 Corinthians 6 in the lesson's explanation of the symbolism of water?

C. To establish that every reference to water in Scripture refers to baptism.
D. To prove that baptism and regeneration are exactly the same event.
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: These passages are cited to demonstrate that water is a biblical metaphor representing the inward, cleansing power of the Holy Spirit rather than a literal physical washing.

Q31. According to Hebrews 12 as explained in the lesson, what is the believer's "new address" or location in the realm of the Spirit?
A. A physical mountain that burns with fire and darkness, similar to Sinai.
B. Mount Zion, the city of the living God, which includes an innumerable company of angels.
C. A literal, geographical recreation of the Garden of Eden in the Middle East.
D. A solitary place where believers must operate completely alone.
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: The speaker cites Hebrews 12:18-22, explaining that believers have not come to a physical mount that can be touched, but rather to "Mount Zion, the city of the living God... And to what? An innumerable company of angels," defining this as the believer's "new environment" and "new address".

Q34. How does the story of Cornelius demonstrate the importance of reverence in attracting angels?
A. Cornelius was a highly educated Jewish priest who studied angelology for years.
B. Cornelius had to be fully born again and filled with the Spirit before an angel would visit him.
C. Even though Cornelius wasn't born again or full of the Spirit at the time, his genuine fear and reverence for the Lord created a conducive environment for angelic visitation.
D. Cornelius learned a secret chant from a herbalist to summon an angel.
ANSWER: C
EXPLANATION: The speaker uses Cornelius as an example of reverence, noting that although he wasn't born again or full of the Spirit at the time, the Bible says he was "one who feared the Lord with his household," proving that "just the fear of the Lord" and genuine reverence creates an environment for angels.

Q41. According to the lesson, what significant event happened around 312 AD that changed the course of Christian history?
A. The Apostle Paul was executed in Rome.
B. Emperor Nero blamed Christians for the Great Fire of Rome.
C. Emperor Constantine had a vision of a cross in the sky, embraced Christianity, and later issued the Edict of Milan to legalize the faith.
D. The Council of Nicaea officially established the New Testament canon.
ANSWER: C
EXPLANATION: The transcript states that in "312 AD when Constantine... saw a cross in the sky and heard the words in this sign, conquer... he became the first Roman Emperor to embrace Christianity," leading to the Edict of Milan in 313 AD which legalized the faith.

Q42. What was the core belief of the heresy known as "Docetism"?
A. That Jesus only seemed human, and that His body, suffering, and death were all illusions because He was pure spirit.
B. That Jesus was a regular human who achieved divinity through good works.
C. That the God of the Old Testament was evil and different from the God of the New Testament.
D. That believers must be physically circumcised to receive salvation.
ANSWER: A
EXPLANATION: The lesson defines Docetism as "the belief that Jesus only seemed human, that his body, his suffering, his death were all illusions. Proponents said he was pure spirit, untouched by physical power".

B. The Council of Trent.
C. The Great Schism, which divided the Eastern Orthodox Church and the Roman Catholic Church.

Q44. What are two early, significant biblical connections between Africa and the Christian narrative mentioned in the lesson?
A. The conversion of the Apostle Paul in Egypt and the writing of the Book of Revelation in Carthage.
B. The flight of Joseph, Mary, and infant Jesus to Egypt, and Simon of Cyrene carrying the cross of Jesus.
C. The construction of the first monastery in Sudan and the translation of the Bible into Swahili.
D. The missionary journeys of Peter to Ethiopia and John to Libya.
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: The transcript highlights that the first significant connection happened when "Joseph, Mary and the infant Jesus fled to Egypt" (Matthew 2:13). Another presence is "Simon of Cyrene, a man from eastern Libya who was compelled to carry the cross of Jesus".

Q45. How did the abolition of the transatlantic slave trade impact the spread of Christianity in West Africa?
A. It caused European missionaries to completely abandon West Africa.
B. It led rescued Africans, such as the Yoruba who settled in Sierra Leone (the "Saroz"), to embrace Christianity and return to their homelands as missionaries.
C. It forced African rulers to revert entirely to traditional religions.
D. It resulted in the immediate translation of the Bible into all 500 Nigerian languages.
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: The speaker explains that the abolition of the slave trade gave the movement wings. "Rescued Africans. Many Yoruba settled in Sierra Leone, Embraced Christianity and returned home as missionaries. These were the Saroz," leading to figures like Bishop Samuel Ajayi Crowther.
REF: EARLY-CHURCH-III-Celebration-Church-International-LMS-mp4-29efed0f-8465.md (05:13-06:37)

Q46. What was the significance of Josiah Olunowo Oshitelu's "Church of the Lord Aladura" founded in 1925?
A. It was a European missionary strategy designed to control local populations.
B. It successfully prevented the spread of Islam in northern Nigeria.
C. It represented an authentically African response to faith, emphasizing healings, visions, and fervent prayer, independent of European invention.
D. It translated the first complete Bible into the Yoruba language.
ANSWER: C
EXPLANATION: The lesson highlights that the Aladura churches were not European inventions. They were "authentically African responses to faith... known for their white garments and deep emphasis on healings, visions and fervent prayer".
REF: EARLY-CHURCH-III-Celebration-Church-International-LMS-mp4-29efed0f-8465.md (09:20-10:39)

Q47. What specific event in 1985 catalyzed the formation of the Pentecostal Fellowship of Nigeria (PFN)?
A. The burning of 152 churches during the Kafanchan crisis.
B. The arrival of Pa Sidney Granville Elton from England.
C. Reverend Uma Ukpai's Greater Lagos Crusade of thanks, which had an overwhelming turnout of prayer volunteers.
D. The first publication of a Yoruba newspaper by Reverend Henry Townsend.
ANSWER: C

C. To renew the church spiritually, reform the clergy, clarify doctrine at the Council of Trent, and spread Catholicism globally through new orders like the Jesuits.
D. To forcibly integrate Protestant teachings into the official Catholic catechism.
ANSWER: C
EXPLANATION: The lesson states that in response to the Protestant Reformation, the Catholic Church launched the Counter Reformation. The key to this revival was "The Council of Trent clarified Catholic doctrine and reformed the clergy. New religious orders, like the Jesuits... took on the mission of spreading Catholicism worldwide".

Q80. How did the Atlantic slave trade create a major contradiction for early Portuguese Christian missions in the Kingdom of Congo?

B. Priests became complicit in the trade, and the church actively profited from baptizing enslaved people.

Q84. What tragic events highlight the severe religious tensions and persecution faced by Christians in Nigeria since the late 1970s?

Q85. What does the term "reverse mission" refer to in the context of modern African Christianity?

Q86. What is the difference between baptism by sprinkling and baptism by pouring?
A. Pouring is exclusively done in rivers, while sprinkling is done in churches.
B. Sprinkling uses anointing oil, while pouring uses regular water.
C. Sprinkling was reserved for adults, while pouring was designed for infants.
D. Pouring essentially uses more water than sprinkling, often involving pouring a basin of water over the head while standing or sitting.
ANSWER: D
EXPLANATION: The speaker explains the difference in modes: "baptism by pouring. And essentially the difference is more water is used... you are made to stand still or sit, and then they carry a basin... and then pour water on your head".

Q88. Why does the Roman Catholic Church practice infant baptism, according to their Catechism?
A. To officially register the child's birth with the state government.
B. Because they believe infants inherit original sin, and baptism washes it away, removing disdain and bringing them into grace.
C. To dedicate the child's future career entirely to the church.

Q90. What specific belief separates the Reformed view of baptism from the Baptist view regarding the subjects of baptism?
A. The Reformed view insists on full immersion, while Baptists allow sprinkling.
B. The Reformed view teaches baptism actively saves the soul, while Baptists teach it does not.
C. The Reformed view practices infant baptism (viewing them as covenant members), whereas the Baptist view strictly requires personal faith and confession, practicing only believer's baptism.
D. The Reformed view requires three years of baptismal classes, while Baptists require none.
ANSWER: C
EXPLANATION: The speaker notes the Reformed view does not believe baptism saves, but they still "believe infant baptism... infants of believing parents are baptized as covenant members." In contrast, the Baptist view states: "Are infants to be baptized? No. Baptism requires personal faith and confession. Only believers are baptized".

Q91. What was Martin Luther's core realization that sparked the Protestant Reformation?
A. That justification does not come by paying money for indulgences or by human works, but by faith alone ("the just shall live by faith").
B. That the Bible should only be read and taught in Latin.
C. That the church urgently needed to build more monasteries to preserve knowledge.
D. That infant baptism was entirely unbiblical and must be stopped immediately.
ANSWER: A
EXPLANATION: The speaker explains that Luther discovered the Catholic Church had moved from biblical positions (like selling indulgences for forgiveness). Luther read "the just shall live by faith" and realized that "justification does not come by paying any money... It comes by faith".

Q92. According to the Naked Bible Podcast reference, how did Old Testament circumcision relate to the community, providing a parallel for infant baptism arguments?

Q93. How did Jesus use "thirst" as a metaphor for salvation in John 7:37?
A. To describe the intense physical dehydration of walking in the desert without water.
B. To illustrate that when a person receives the Holy Spirit, nothing else defines satisfaction greater than that.
C. To prove that physical water baptism is an absolute requirement for salvation.
D. To demand that His followers drink only water and abstain from wine.
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: The speaker lists "thirst" as a metaphor of salvation alongside poverty. Quoting John 7:37 ("if anyone thirsts, let him come to me and drink"), he explains, "why was hunger and thirst used? Because when you receive the Holy Spirit, when you are born again, nothing else defines satisfaction greater than that".

Q95. According to historical trends mentioned in the lesson, how did the preparation for baptism change from the first century to the third century?
A. It remained immediate upon profession of faith throughout all three centuries.
B. It shifted from immediate baptism in the first century, to basic instruction in the second, to a formal three-year preparation in the third century.
C. It shifted from a three-year requirement in the first century to immediate baptism in the third.
D. Preparation was banned completely by the third century to encourage mass conversions.
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: The speaker outlines the progression: "in the first century... Immediate baptism on profession of faith... in the second century. Basic instruction was added in the Didache... in the third century, there was now more emphasis on preparation... And this formal preparation took three years".

Q98. What practical standard does the speaker suggest implementing for future water baptisms to ensure the candidate's genuine conversion?
A. Requiring them to pay a nominal baptismal fee.
B. Requiring someone to vouch for the individual's character and profession of faith.
C. Requiring a comprehensive written theology exam.
D. Requiring them to fast for seven continuous days.
ANSWER: B

Q99. In the lesson's explanation of 1 Peter 3, what did the flood of Noah accomplish besides preserving humanity?
A. It provided necessary water for post-flood agriculture.
B. It acted as a judgment on rebel spirits (fallen angels) and their giant offspring.
C. It washed away the original sin of the surviving animals.
D. It created the physical boundaries of the Mediterranean Sea.
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: The speaker explains that the flood was "actually the preservation of mankind and judgment on all those rebel spirits and their children. And so the flood judged them." Baptism now acts as a demonstration separating the believer from those judged spirits.

Q100. Why does the speaker reject the argument that the baptism of entire "households" (like the Philippian jailer's) proves infant baptism?
A. Because the jailer was explicitly stated in scripture to have no children.
B. Because arguing that infants were present in the household is an argument from silence and mere "gymnastics."
C. Because the jailer was a Roman soldier and couldn't legally have a family.
D. Because the jailer's household only included his adult servants.
ANSWER: B
EXPLANATION: The speaker refutes infant baptism by addressing the "household" argument: "many of the people who argue for it argue from silence... he asked, what shall. What can I do to be saved? And he said, believe... you and your house. And so now they argue on silence from silence that if it was here in his house, they were probably infants... it's just gymnastics".
REF: BAPTISM-V-Celebration-Church-International-LMS-mp4-145d20c7-d8f1.md (12:33-13:31)
